+# ACT: Automatically Generating Compiler Backends from Tensor Accelerator ISA Descriptions
+
+This is the artifact for our paper on automatically generating sound and complete compiler backends for tensor accelerators from their ISA descriptions written in TAIDL.
+
+This artifact consists of ACT source code, TAIDL ISA definitions, input kernel benchmarks, and the necessary scripts to reproduce the evaluation results.
+To facilitate artifact evaluation, we have automated the entire environment setup and experimental processes as part of Docker images.
+
+## System Requirements
+
+**Docker**
+
+We use Docker images for environment setup of ACT and baselines.
+To run the ACT artifact, install Docker using the [installation guide](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/).
+
+**Architecture Support**
+
+- **amd64/x86_64** is fully supported.
+- On **arm64**, the ACT image and Steps 0-1 work; Step 2 requires amd64 due to baseline dependencies (e.g., Gemmini, Chipyard) that are not available for arm64.
+
+## ACT Artifact Overview
+
+### Scripts
+
+The `scripts/` directory contains the following bash scripts to automate the experimental workflows:
+
+- `setup.sh` - pull the ACT Docker image from Docker Hub, or build either image locally.
+- `kick-tires.sh` - compile the QKV running example end to end and regenerate all paper figures from the paper's benchmarking data.
+- `full.sh` - run ACT compiler backends on every benchmark kernel along with the baselines.
+- `clean.sh` - remove all files generated including the log files and PDF plots.
+
+### Docker Images
+
+| Docker image                                      | Environment installed                                                                                    | Architecture | Dockerfile                               |
+| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
+| `devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:amd64`          | ACT (Rust, OR-Tools, Python) and the plotting toolchain                                                  | amd64        | `docker/artifact-act/Dockerfile.amd64` |
+| `devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:arm64`          | ACT (Rust, OR-Tools, Python) and the plotting toolchain                                                  | arm64        | `docker/artifact-act/Dockerfile.arm64` |
+| `devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:baseline-amd64` | Everything in the ACT image, plus Gemmini RTL simulation (Chipyard, Verilator) and the AWS NKI simulator | amd64        | `docker/artifact-baseline/Dockerfile`  |
+
+The ACT image is pulled from Docker Hub and is all that Step 1 needs.
+The baseline image is the complete evaluation environment used by Step 2.
+
+### Generated PDF Plots and CSV Data Files
+
+`plots/paper_data/` contains the paper's benchmarking data as CSV, and is where the figures are written.
+
+Figures:
+
+- `perf-summary.pdf` - Figure 20: compilation coverage for AWS NKI, and geomean speedup of the compiled code
+- `perf-gemmini.pdf` - Figure 21: speedup of ACT-Gemmini over the Exo library and over the Gemmini SW library
+- `compilation_time.pdf` - Figure 23: breakdown of compilation time for ACT-Gemmini and ACT-NKI
+- `perf-gemmini-appendix.pdf` - Appendix G: speedup over the Gemmini SW library, and relative data movement
+
+Tables:
+
+- `nki_coverage.csv` - Per-kernel compilation status and speedup for the TPUGraphs kernels
+- `gemmini_exo_perf.csv` - Appendix F: cycle counts for every loop-fission factor of the six Exo GEMM shapes
+- `gemmini_swlib_perf.csv` - Cycle counts of ACT-Gemmini and the Gemmini SW library, per kernel
+- `amx_perf.csv` - Per-kernel speedup of ACT-AMX over the oneDNN library
+- `gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv`, `nki_stress_compile.csv` - Raw data for the compilation time figure
+- `gemmini_data_movement.csv` - Scratchpad traffic in bytes for the composite kernels
+
+## Step-by-Step Instructions to Reproduce Results
+
+### (Step 0) Setup the Docker Environment
+
+This will pull the ACT Docker image from Docker Hub.
+This should only take a few minutes.
+
+Run the setup script using:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/setup.sh
+```
+
+Alternatively, you can build the image locally using:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/setup.sh --build
+```
+
+### (Step 1) Kick the Tires: QKV End-to-End and Quick Plot Generation
+
+This generates the QKV compiler backend from its TAIDL ISA specification, builds it, and compiles the QKV attention kernel to accelerator assembly.
+It then uses the paper's benchmarking data (`plots/paper_data/`) to regenerate all figures.
+This should only take a few minutes to run.
+
+Run the kick-tires script using:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/kick-tires.sh
+```
+
+Outputs:
+
+- `compiled_asm/qkv/qkv.asm.py` - QKV accelerator assembly emitted by ACT
+- `plots/paper_data/*.pdf` - all paper figures, redrawn from the paper's benchmarking data
+
+### (Step 2) Full Evaluation with Baselines
+
+This step needs the baseline image (`baseline-amd64`), which adds the Gemmini RTL simulator (Chipyard, Verilator) and the AWS NKI simulator on top of the ACT toolchain.
+It is pulled or built from `docker/artifact-baseline/Dockerfile`, and is set up once and reused:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/setup.sh --full
+```
+
+Building it locally (`--full --build`) compiles Chipyard, the RISC-V toolchain, and Verilator from source.
+It can take a few hours depending on the machine, and needs at least 60 GB of free disk.
+
+`full.sh` then generates every compiler backend from its TAIDL ISA specification, compiles all benchmark kernels, and measures the compiled code against the baselines.
+
+Run the full script using:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/full.sh
+```
+
+A default run takes under ten minutes and prints a stage summary when it finishes.
+Most of it is ACT-Gemmini (115 kernels compiled and 30 RTL simulations, about 4 minutes) and ACT-NKI (1055 kernels compiled and validated, about 3 minutes).
+
+For every full run, a new folder is created as `plots/full_run_<timestamp>/` containing the generated PDF plots and CSV data files.
+The tables in `plots/paper_data/` are copied into that folder and the measured rows are updated there, so the paper's data is left untouched.
+
+Three stages are long enough to be opt-in:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/full.sh --regen-kernels       # also regenerate the TPUGraphs and NNSmith kernels (five minutes)
+./scripts/full.sh --rerun-neuronxcc     # also recompile the TPUGraphs kernels with neuronx-cc (doubles the NKI stage)
+./scripts/full.sh --rerun-exo-sweep     # also re-measure all 112 Exo loop-fission variants (more than a day)
+```
+
+Pass `-j N` to set the number of parallel simulator jobs; by default it uses all but two of the available cores.
+
+### (Optional) Cleanup/Fresh Start
+
+To remove all generated files including log files and PDF plots, run:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/clean.sh
+```
+

+

+
+The evaluation in the paper makes three key claims, and this artifact reproduces all of them.
+

+| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

+

+
+### (C1) Compilation Coverage

+## Reusability Guide
+
+ACT is not tied to the accelerators evaluated in the paper: a new compiler backend is generated from a TAIDL ISA specification alone, with no changes to the compilation algorithm.
+`REUSABILITY.md` defines a custom ISA end to end, compiles a kernel with the generated backend, and documents the TAIDL API and the backend command-line interface.
+Further tutorials are available in the public ACT repository at [https://github.com/act-compiler/act](https://github.com/act-compiler/act).

+# Getting Started with ACT
+
+ACT generates a complete compiler backend for a tensor accelerator from its ISA description written in TAIDL.
+The generated backend is a standalone binary that takes tiled XLA-HLO kernels as input and emits accelerator assembly, and no part of the compilation algorithm is specific to the accelerators evaluated in the paper.
+
+This guide uses the QKV running example, whose ISA description is `accelerators/qkv.py` and whose kernel is `kernels/qkv/qkv.hlo`.
+It is the same specification that `./scripts/kick-tires.sh` compiles end to end, so every command below can be run after Step 0 of `README.md`.
+
+All commands below run inside the ACT Docker image, with this repository mounted at `/act`:
+
+```bash
+docker run --rm -it -v "$(pwd):/act" -w /act -e PYTHONPATH=/act \
+    devanshdvj/act-oopsla26-artifact:amd64 bash
+```
+
+On arm64, use the `arm64` tag instead.
+
+## Writing Custom ISAs in TAIDL
+
+#### 1. Define the Data Models
+
+An accelerator is an `act.taidl.Accelerator`, and each of its memories is a data model.
+The off-chip memory `d0` is added automatically as a flat `u8` buffer, so only the on-chip memories are declared.
+
+```python
+# accelerators/qkv.py
+from act.taidl import Accelerator
+from act.generator import generate_backend
+
+qkv = Accelerator("QKV")
+
+# d1: 128 rows x 64 columns of bf16
+qkv.add_data_model("d1", [128], [64], "bf16")
+
+# d2: 64 rows x 64 columns of bf16
+qkv.add_data_model("d2", [64], [64], "bf16")
+```
+
+The second argument is the addressable dimensions of the memory and the third is the unit dimensions held at each address, so `d1` holds 128 addressable vectors of 64 `bf16` elements.
+A memory that is addressed along every dimension declares them all as addressable, as the Gemmini scratchpad and accumulator do:
+
+```python
+# accelerators/gemmini.py
+gemmini.add_data_model("spad", [1024 * 16, 16], [], "s8")
+gemmini.add_data_model("acc", [64 * 16, 16], [], "s32")
+```
+
+#### 2. Define the Instructions
+
+Each instruction declares two kinds of attributes: computational attributes, which change what the instruction computes, and addressing attributes, which only select where its operands live.
+`set_inputs` and `set_outputs` describe the operands as `[data model, [address], [shape]]`, and `add_semantics` gives the exact semantics of the instruction as an XLA-HLO computation.
+
+```python
+# (1) load_rm: Loads data from HBM (d0) in row-major format to d1
+instr = qkv.add_instruction("load_rm", ["n"], ["addr_in", "addr_out"])
+instr.set_inputs([["d0", ["@a.addr_in"], ["@c.n * 128"]]])  # u8[@c.n * 128]
+instr.set_outputs([["d1", ["@a.addr_out"], ["@c.n"]]])  # bf16[@c.n, 64]
+instr.add_semantics("""
+ENTRY load_rm {
+    %In1 = u8[`@c.n * 128`] parameter(0);
+    %a = u8[`@c.n`,64,2] reshape(%In1);
+    ROOT %Out0 = bf16[`@c.n`,64] bitcast_convert(%a);
+}
+""")
+```
+
+`@c.<name>` refers to a computational attribute and `@a.<name>` to an addressing attribute, and expressions over them are written between backticks.
+Inside the semantics, `%In1`, `%In2`, ... are the inputs in the order they were declared, and the root of the computation is the output `%Out0`.
+The search that ACT performs is driven entirely by these semantics, which is what makes the generated backend sound and complete for the ISA as described.
+
+An instruction that overwrites one of its operands marks that operand as in-place, which lets the backend reuse the same address for the result:
+
+```python
+# accelerators/gemmini.py
+instr = gemmini.add_instruction("mvin_acc_low_add", ["rows", "cols", "scale"], ["hbm_addr", "acc_addr"])
+instr.set_inputs([["acc", ["@a.acc_addr", 0], ["@c.rows", "@c.cols"]],
+                  ["d0", ["@a.hbm_addr"], ["@c.rows * @c.cols"]]])
+instr.set_outputs([["acc", ["@a.acc_addr", 0], ["@c.rows", "@c.cols"]]])
+instr.set_inplace([True, False])
+```
+
+#### 3. Generate the Compiler Backend
+
+A specification ends with `generate_backend(qkv)`, so running it generates and builds the backend:
+
+```bash
+python accelerators/qkv.py
+```
+
+This emits the backend sources under `accelerators/targets/QKV/`, builds them with `cargo build --release`, and installs the binary at `accelerators/backends/QKV`:
+
+```
+      ACT-QKV built | 15s
+```
+
+#### 4. Write Kernels
+
+Input kernels are tiled XLA-HLO modules whose tile shapes match the data models of the accelerator.
+
+```
+// kernels/qkv/qkv.hlo
+HloModule qkv_attention, entry_computation_layout={(bf16[64,64]{1,0}, bf16[64,64]{1,0}, bf16[64,64]{1,0})->bf16[64,64]{1,0}}
+
+// Helper function for reduce_sum
+%reduce_add (x: bf16[], y: bf16[]) -> bf16[] {
+  %x = bf16[] parameter(0)
+  %y = bf16[] parameter(1)
+  ROOT %sum = bf16[] add(%x, %y)
+}
+
+ENTRY main {
+  // Input tensors
+  %q = bf16[64,64] parameter(0)
+  %k = bf16[64,64] parameter(1)
+  %v = bf16[64,64] parameter(2)
+
+  // Step 1: Compute attention scores S = Q × K^T
+  %k_transpose = bf16[64,64] transpose(%k), dimensions={1,0}
+  %scores = bf16[64,64] dot(%q, %k_transpose), lhs_contracting_dims={1}, rhs_contracting_dims={0}
+
+  // Step 2: Apply softmax normalization
+  %scores_exp = bf16[64,64] exponential(%scores)
+
+  %zero = bf16[] constant(0)
+  %sum = bf16[64] reduce(%scores_exp, %zero), dimensions={1}, to_apply=%reduce_add
+
+  %sum_broadcast = bf16[64,64] broadcast(%sum), dimensions={0}
+  %probs = bf16[64,64] divide(%scores_exp, %sum_broadcast)
+
+  // Step 3: Compute weighted sum O = P × V
+  ROOT %output = bf16[64,64] dot(%probs, %v), lhs_contracting_dims={1}, rhs_contracting_dims={0}
+}
+```
+
+#### 5. Compile the Kernels
+
+The generated backend takes one kernel and writes one assembly file:
+
+```bash
+./accelerators/backends/QKV --input kernels/qkv/qkv.hlo --output compiled_asm/qkv/qkv.asm.py
+```
+
+The emitted assembly is a `@kernel`-decorated function.
+The decorator records the HBM footprint and the input, constant and output tensors of the kernel, and each `api.<instruction>` call is one instruction of the ISA with its attributes bound:
+
+```python
+# compiled_asm/qkv/qkv.asm.py
+def qkv_attention(kernel, api):
+    @kernel(hbm=32768,
+            input=[
+                {'addr': 0, 'shape': (64, 64), 'dtype': jnp.bfloat16},
+                {'addr': 8192, 'shape': (64, 64), 'dtype': jnp.bfloat16},
+                {'addr': 16384, 'shape': (64, 64), 'dtype': jnp.bfloat16},
+            ],
+            constant=[],
+            output=[
+                {'addr': 24576, 'shape': (64, 64), 'dtype': jnp.bfloat16},
+            ]
+            )
+    def qkv_attention_():
+        api.load_rm(n = 64, addr_in = 0, addr_out = 64)
+        api.load_cm(n = 64, addr_in = 8192, addr_out = 0)
+        api.gemm(addr_1 = 64, addr_2 = 0, addr_out = 0)
+        api.softmax(n = 64, addr = 0)
+        api.mov(n = 64, addr_in = 0, addr_out = 64)
+        api.load_rm(n = 64, addr_in = 16384, addr_out = 0)
+        api.gemm(addr_1 = 64, addr_2 = 0, addr_out = 0)
+        api.mov(n = 64, addr_in = 0, addr_out = 0)
+        api.store_rm(n = 64, addr_in = 0, addr_out = 24576)
+
+    return qkv_attention_
+```
+
+#### 6. Inspect a Compilation
+
+`--stats` reports the search statistics and the per-phase timings of the two compilation phases on stdout:
+
+```
+[STATS] total_time=21.83ms
+[STATS] rewrite_iterations=3
+[STATS] egraph_nodes=118
+[STATS] candidates_generated=15
+[STATS] best_cost=32
+[STATS] best_found_at=10.71ms
+[STATS] M1_Initializer=0.067ms (1 calls)
+[STATS] M2_Rewriter=0.205ms (3 calls)
+[STATS] M3_Extractor=1.388ms (9 calls)
+[STATS] M4_TopoSort=0.649ms (15 calls)
+[STATS] M5_CSPGen=1.017ms (15 calls)
+[STATS] MX_Solver=1.364ms (15 calls)
+[STATS] M6_Emitter=1.701ms (15 calls)
+[STATS] MC_CostModel=0.379ms (15 calls)
+```
+
+`--log <dir>` keeps the intermediates of the compilation in `<dir>` instead of a temporary directory: `log.txt`, a `metadata.json` with the input and output specification of the kernel, and a numbered `.pii` and `.py` pair per candidate, holding the instruction sequence the extractor found and the assembly emitted from it.
+`--stop-at-first` returns the first valid assembly instead of searching for the cheapest one.
+
+The exit code of the backend is the compilation result:
+
+| Exit code | Meaning                                            |
+| --------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
+| 0         | assembly written to `--output`                     |
+| 1         | usage or internal error                            |
+| 2         | the extractor produced no candidates               |
+| 3         | the candidates had no ISA instructions             |
+| 4         | in-place validation rejected every candidate       |
+| 5         | the allocation CSP was infeasible for every candidate |
+| 6         | assembly emission failed                           |
+| 7         | the emitted assembly was not parseable             |
+
+On exits 2 to 7 the backend prints a single `Error:` line to stderr naming the input file and the stage that failed.

+## TAIDL API Reference
+
+### `Accelerator`
+
+- `Accelerator(name)` - a new accelerator; the off-chip memory `d0` is added automatically as a flat `u8` buffer.
+- `add_data_model(name, addressable_dims, unit_dims, dtype)` - add an on-chip memory.
+- `add_instruction(name, computational_attrs, addressing_attrs)` - add an instruction and return it.
+
+### `Instruction`
+
+- `set_inputs([[data_model, [address], [shape]], ...])` - the operands read by the instruction.
+- `set_outputs([[data_model, [address], [shape]], ...])` - the operands written by the instruction.
+- `set_inplace([bool, ...])` - mark which inputs the instruction overwrites; one flag per input.
+- `add_semantics(hlo)` - the XLA-HLO semantics of the instruction, parsed immediately.
+
+### Data Types
+
+`s8`, `s16`, `s32`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `f16`, `f32`, `bf16`, `pred`.
+
+### Operations in ISA Semantics
+
+**Element-wise:** `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `power`, `maximum`, `minimum`, `negate`, `abs`, `exp`, `exponential`, `logistic`, `tanh`, `log-plus-one`, `and`, `or`, `xor`, `shift-left`, `shift-right-logical`, `shift-right-arithmetic`.
+
+**Shape and layout:** `reshape`, `transpose`, `slice`, `concatenate`, `broadcast`, `dynamic_update_slice`, `copy`.
+
+**Type:** `convert`, `bitcast_convert`.
+
+**Linear algebra and reductions:** `dot`, `reduce`, `reduce_add`, `reduce_max`, `reduce_and`, `reduce_or`.
+
+**Selection and constants:** `compare`, `select`, `select_lt`, `select_eq_var`, `constant`, `iota`, `parameter`.

+
+This module provides the main interface for generating backend code.
+It coordinates all the individual file generators to produce a complete
+ACT backend implementation.
+"""
+
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+from typing import List
+import subprocess
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from .taidl import Accelerator
+
+from .ir_buffer_rs_generator import generate_buffer_rs_file
+from .ir_egraph_rs_generator import generate_egraph_rs_file
+from .malloc_globals_cc_generator import generate_globals_file
+from .malloc_instructions_h_generator import generate_instructions_file
+from .malloc_parser_cc_generator import generate_parser_file
+from .isel_applier_rs_generator import generate_applier_file
+from .malloc_act_malloc_cc_generator import generate_act_malloc_file
+from .isel_ir2isa_rewrites_txt_generator import generate_ir2isa_rewrites_txt_file
+from .isel_ir2isa_rewrites_rs_generator import generate_ir2isa_rewrites_rs_file
+
+
+@dataclass
+class InstructionMetadata:
+    name: str
+    semantics_ast: object
+    has_comp_attrs: bool
+    comp_attrs: List[str]
+    rhs_size: int
+
+
+def _fmt_elapsed(seconds: float) -> str:
+    """Stage-elapsed style: Xs, Xm YYs, Xh YYm."""
+    s = int(round(seconds))
+    if s < 60:
+        return f"{s}s"
+    if s < 3600:
+        return f"{s // 60}m {s % 60:02d}s"
+    return f"{s // 3600}h {(s % 3600) // 60:02d}m"
+
+
+def _get_instruction_metadata(accelerator: Accelerator) -> List[InstructionMetadata]:
+    """Extract instruction metadata needed for rewrite rule generation"""
+    metadata_list = []
+    for instruction in accelerator.instructions:
+        if instruction.instr_semantics_ast:
+            metadata = InstructionMetadata(
+                name=instruction.instruction,
+                semantics_ast=instruction.instr_semantics_ast,
+                has_comp_attrs=len(instruction.comp_attr) > 0,
+                comp_attrs=list(instruction.comp_attr),
+                rhs_size=len(instruction.instr_inputs) + 1
+            )
+            metadata_list.append(metadata)
+    return metadata_list
+
+
+def generate_backend(accelerator: Accelerator, base_dir: str = None) -> None:
+    """
+    Generate complete ACT backend code for an accelerator.
+
+    Args:
+        accelerator: TAIDL Accelerator object
+        base_dir: Base directory of the project. Defaults to accelerator.base_dir.
+    """
+    if base_dir is None:
+        base_dir = accelerator.base_dir
+
+    # Setup directories
+    target_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, 'targets', accelerator.name)
+    Path(target_dir).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+    generic_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'generic')
+    backend_gen_dir = os.path.join(target_dir, 'backend')
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+
+    # Copy generic backend structure
+    if os.path.exists(backend_gen_dir):
+        shutil.rmtree(backend_gen_dir)
+    shutil.copytree(generic_dir, backend_gen_dir)
+
+    instruction_metadata = _get_instruction_metadata(accelerator)
+
+    # Generate rewrite rules
+    generate_ir2isa_rewrites_txt_file(backend_gen_dir, instruction_metadata)
+
+    # Generate Rust files
+    generate_ir2isa_rewrites_rs_file(backend_gen_dir, instruction_metadata)
+
+    generate_buffer_rs_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.instructions, accelerator.data_model)
+
+    generate_egraph_rs_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.instructions)
+
+    generate_applier_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.instructions)
+
+    # Generate C++ malloc files
+    generate_globals_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.data_model)
+
+    generate_instructions_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.instructions, accelerator.data_model)
+
+    generate_parser_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.instructions)
+
+    generate_act_malloc_file(backend_gen_dir, accelerator.data_model)
+
+    # Build the backend
+    cargo_build_dir = os.path.join(backend_gen_dir, 'target')
+    if os.path.exists(cargo_build_dir):
+        shutil.rmtree(cargo_build_dir)
+    subprocess.run(["cargo", "build", "--release"], cwd=backend_gen_dir,
+                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)
+
+    # Copy built backend to final destination

+        shutil.copy(build_backend_path, final_dest_path)
+        elapsed = _fmt_elapsed(time.perf_counter() - start)
+        print(f"      ACT-{accelerator.name} built | {elapsed}")
+    else:
+        raise RuntimeError("Backend build failed. Please check the build logs.")

+cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
+project(Scheduler LANGUAGES C CXX)
+
+set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
+set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
+
+# List all your source files
+set(SOURCE_FILES
+    src/main.cc
+)
+
+set(LIB_SOURCE_FILES
+    src/act_malloc.cc
+    src/constraint.cc
+    src/emitter.cc
+    src/globals.cc
+    src/parser.cc
+    src/scheduler.cc
+)
+
+set(ORTOOLS_ROOT "/opt/ortools/")
+set(CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH "${ORTOOLS_ROOT}" ${CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH})
+find_package(ortools REQUIRED)
+
+set(JSON_INCLUDE_PATH "/opt/nlohmann_json/include")
+add_library(nlohmann_json INTERFACE)
+target_include_directories(nlohmann_json INTERFACE ${JSON_INCLUDE_PATH})
+
+# Create a static library to be linked with Rust
+add_library(malloc_static STATIC ${LIB_SOURCE_FILES})
+target_link_libraries(malloc_static PUBLIC ortools::ortools)
+target_link_libraries(malloc_static PUBLIC nlohmann_json)
+target_include_directories(malloc_static PRIVATE include)
+
+# Also create an executable for debugging/testing

+        super().__init__()
+        self.assignments = []
+        self.root_assignment = None
+        self.comp_attributes = set()
+        self.variable_definitions = {}
+        self.variable_usage = set()
+
+    def visitModule(self, ctx):
+        self.visitChildren(ctx)
+
+        self.assignments = self._compute_traversal_order()
+
+        if self.root_assignment:
+            for assignment in self.assignments:
+                if assignment['lhs'] == self.root_assignment['lhs']:
+                    self.root_assignment = assignment
+                    break
+
+        return {
+            'assignments': self.assignments,
+            'root_assignment': self.root_assignment,
+            'comp_attributes': list(self.comp_attributes)
+        }
+
+    def _compute_traversal_order(self):
+        """Reorder self.assignments to match the left-subtree-first postorder that
+        egg's pattern parser produces from the RHS pattern text (isel_ir2isa_rewrites_txt_generator's
+        RewriteRuleVisitor). find_matches (act/generic/src/isel/rewrites/applier.rs) walks the
+        parsed pattern this way at runtime, so operand indices must follow it rather than
+        declaration order.
+        """
+        if not self.root_assignment:
+            return self.assignments
+
+        # Match RewriteRuleVisitor: first use takes the original, later uses a `_dup`.
+        non_dup_in_order = [a for a in self.assignments if not a['lhs'].endswith('_dup')]
+        usage_seen = set()
+        resolved_operands = {}
+        for assignment in non_dup_in_order:
+            resolved = []
+            for operand in assignment['operands']:
+                if operand in self.variable_definitions and operand in usage_seen:
+                    dup_name = f"{operand}_dup"
+                    resolved.append(dup_name if dup_name in self.variable_definitions else operand)
+                else:
+                    resolved.append(operand)
+                    usage_seen.add(operand)
+            resolved_operands[assignment['lhs']] = resolved
+
+        output = []
+        visited = set()
+
+        def visit(name):
+            if name in visited:
+                return
+            visited.add(name)
+            assignment = self.assignments[self.variable_definitions[name]]
+
+            if name.endswith('_dup'):
+                # Duplicated subtrees carry duplicated children.
+                children = []
+                for operand in assignment['operands']:
+                    if operand not in self.variable_definitions:
+                        continue
+                    dup_name = f"{operand}_dup"
+                    children.append(dup_name if dup_name in self.variable_definitions else operand)
+            else:
+                children = [op for op in resolved_operands.get(name, assignment['operands'])
+                            if op in self.variable_definitions]
+
+            for child in children:
+                visit(child)
+            output.append(assignment)
+
+        visit(self.root_assignment['lhs'])
+        return output
+
+    def visitInstruction(self, ctx):
+        lhs_name = ctx.IDENTIFIER().getText()
+        op_name = ctx.OPERATION().getText()
+        result_type_info = self.visit(ctx.result_type())
+        lhs_type, lhs_shape = result_type_info
+
+        is_root = ctx.ROOT() is not None
+
+        self._extract_comp_attrs_from_text(lhs_shape)
+
+        operand_names = []
+        operand_texts = []
+        if ctx.operands():
+            operands = self.visit(ctx.operands())
+            for operand_text, operand_type in operands:
+                self._extract_comp_attrs_from_text(operand_text)
+                operand_texts.append(operand_text)
+                if operand_type == 'IDENTIFIER':
+                    operand_names.append(operand_text)
+
+        for operand_text in operand_names:
+            if operand_text in self.variable_definitions:
+                if operand_text in self.variable_usage:
+                    self._duplicate_variable_recursive(operand_text)
+                else:
+                    self.variable_usage.add(operand_text)
+
+        # A literal-bounds slice pins the matched OpSlice payload; @c. bounds stay wildcard.
+        slice_payload = None
+        # An iota matches along one axis only, so its dimension is pinned too.
+        iota_dim = None
+        if ctx.attributes():
+            attributes = self.visit(ctx.attributes())
+            for _, attr_value, attr_type in attributes:
+                if attr_type in ['EXPRESSION', 'BRACELIST']:
+                    self._extract_comp_attrs_from_text(str(attr_value))
+                elif attr_type == 'SLICELIST' and op_name == 'slice':
+                    slice_payload = canonical_slice_payload(attr_value)
+                elif attr_type == 'INT' and op_name == 'iota':
+                    iota_dim = str(attr_value).strip()
+
+        # A literal constant pins the matched value; a `@c.` one is a comp attr.
+        const_literal = None
+        if op_name == 'constant' and operand_texts and '@c.' not in operand_texts[0]:
+            const_literal = operand_texts[0].strip()
+
+        assignment = {
+            'lhs': lhs_name,
+            'dtype': lhs_type,
+            'shape': lhs_shape,
+            'operands': operand_names,
+            'operand_texts': operand_texts,
+            'slice_payload': slice_payload,
+            'iota_dim': iota_dim,
+            'const_literal': const_literal,
+        }
+
+        self.variable_definitions[lhs_name] = len(self.assignments)
+        self.assignments.append(assignment)
+
+        if is_root:
+            self.root_assignment = assignment
+
+        return assignment
+
+    def _duplicate_variable_recursive(self, var_name):
+        dup_name = f"{var_name}_dup"
+
+        if dup_name in self.variable_definitions:
+            return
+
+        original = self.assignments[self.variable_definitions[var_name]]
+
+        for operand in original['operands']:
+            if operand in self.variable_definitions:
+                self._duplicate_variable_recursive(operand)
+
+        duplicate = {
+            'lhs': dup_name,
+            'dtype': original['dtype'],
+            'shape': original['shape'],
+            'operands': original['operands'],
+            'slice_payload': original.get('slice_payload'),
+            'const_literal': original.get('const_literal'),
+        }
+        self.variable_definitions[dup_name] = len(self.assignments)
+        self.assignments.append(duplicate)
+
+    def _extract_comp_attrs_from_text(self, text):
+        pattern = r'@c\.(\w+)'
+        matches = re.findall(pattern, str(text))
+        self.comp_attributes.update(matches)
+
+    def visitResult_type(self, ctx):
+        shape_info = self.visit(ctx.shape())
+        shape_dims, shape_type = shape_info
+        return (shape_type, shape_dims)
+
+    def visitShape(self, ctx):
+        dims = ctx.getText()
+        typ = ctx.parentCtx.TYPE().getText()
+        return (dims, typ)
+
+    def visitOperands(self, ctx):
+        operand_list = []
+        for operand_ctx in ctx.operand():
+            operand_info = self.visit(operand_ctx)
+            operand_list.append(operand_info)
+        return operand_list
+
+    def visitOperand(self, ctx):
+        value_ctx = ctx.value()
+        value_text = value_ctx.getText()
+
+        if value_ctx.INT():
+            operand_type = 'INT'
+        elif value_ctx.IDENTIFIER():
+            operand_type = 'IDENTIFIER'
+        elif value_ctx.EXPRESSION():
+            operand_type = 'EXPRESSION'
+        else:
+            operand_type = 'UNKNOWN'
+
+        return (value_text, operand_type)
+
+    def visitAttributes(self, ctx):
+        attributes_list = []
+        for attribute_ctx in ctx.attribute():
+            attr_info = self.visit(attribute_ctx)
+            attributes_list.append(attr_info)
+        return attributes_list
+
+    def visitAttribute(self, ctx):
+        # an attribute name may lex as OPERATION, e.g. slice=
+        attr_name = (ctx.IDENTIFIER() or ctx.OPERATION()).getText()
+        attr_value_info = self.visit(ctx.attributeValue())
+        attr_value, attr_type = attr_value_info
+        return (attr_name, attr_value, attr_type)
+
+    def visitAttributeValue(self, ctx):
+        if ctx.braceList():
+            brace_info = self.visit(ctx.braceList())
+            return (brace_info, 'BRACELIST')
+        elif ctx.sliceList():
+            return (self.visit(ctx.sliceList()), 'SLICELIST')
+        elif ctx.value():
+            value_ctx = ctx.value()
+            value_text = value_ctx.getText()
+
+            if value_ctx.INT():
+                value_type = 'INT'
+            elif value_ctx.IDENTIFIER():
+                value_type = 'IDENTIFIER'
+            elif value_ctx.EXPRESSION():
+                value_type = 'EXPRESSION'
+            else:
+                value_type = 'UNKNOWN'
+
+            return (value_text, value_type)
+        else:
+            return ("", "UNKNOWN")
+
+    def visitSliceList(self, ctx):
+        """Group the flat `[ start : end (: stride)? ]` tokens into per-dim bound lists."""
+        dims = []
+        for child in ctx.getChildren():
+            text = child.getText()
+            if text == '[':
+                dims.append([])
+            elif text == ']' or text in (':', ',', '{', '}'):
+                continue
+            elif dims:
+                dims[-1].append(text)
+        return dims
+
+
+def canonical_slice_payload(dims):
+    """Serialize literal slice bounds as add_slice does: `start:end` per dim, joined by ';'.
+
+    Returns None when any bound references a computational attribute.
+    """
+    if not dims:
+        return None
+    parts = []
+    for bounds in dims:
+        if len(bounds) < 2:
+            return None
+        start = bounds[0].replace('`', '').replace(' ', '')
+        end = bounds[1].replace('`', '').replace(' ', '')
+        if '@c.' in start or '@c.' in end:
+            return None
+        parts.append(f"{start}:{end}")
+    return ';'.join(parts)

+def map_dtype_to_rust(dtype):
+    dtype_map = {
+        'u8': 'Dtype::U8',
+        's8': 'Dtype::I8',
+        'u16': 'Dtype::U16',
+        's16': 'Dtype::I16',
+        'u32': 'Dtype::U32',
+        's32': 'Dtype::I32',
+        'u64': 'Dtype::U64',
+        's64': 'Dtype::I64',
+        'f16': 'Dtype::FP16',
+        'f32': 'Dtype::FP32',
+        'f64': 'Dtype::FP64',
+        'bf16': 'Dtype::BF16',
+        'pred': 'Dtype::Pred',
+    }
+
+    rust_type = dtype_map.get(dtype)
+    assert (rust_type != None)
+    return rust_type

+def parse_comp_attr_expression(shape_expr, comp_attr):
+    # Only works with @c.attr or @c.attr * constant
+    # Very fragile but should work
+    if not comp_attr or f'@c.{comp_attr}' not in shape_expr:
+        return comp_attr, []
+
+    expr = shape_expr.replace('`', '').replace(' ', '')
+    pattern = f'@c.{comp_attr}'
+
+    if f'{pattern}*' in expr:
+        start = expr.index(pattern) + len(pattern) + 1
+        factor_str = ''
+        for char in expr[start:]:
+            if char.isdigit():
+                factor_str += char
+            else:
+                break
+        if factor_str:
+            return comp_attr, [int(factor_str)]
+
+    return comp_attr, []
+

+def generate_all_comp_attr_extractions(root_assignment, comp_attrs, all_assignments,
+                                        need_check, templates):
+    if not comp_attrs or not root_assignment:
+        return ""
+
+    num_assignments = len(all_assignments)
+    parts = []
+
+    for attr in comp_attrs:
+        found = False
+        # Case 1: attr appears alone in a shape dimension (e.g. `@c.rows` in `@c.rows,@c.cols`)
+        for i, assignment in enumerate(all_assignments):
+            shape = assignment['shape']
+            if f'@c.{attr}' in shape:
+                dim_index = _find_dim_index_for_attr(shape, attr)
+                if dim_index < 0:
+                    continue
+                _, factors = parse_comp_attr_expression(shape, attr)
+                division = ""
+                if factors:
+                    division_factor = 1
+                    for f in factors:
+                        division_factor *= f
+                    division = f" / {division_factor}"
+                if need_check:
+                    shape_template = "ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.attr_from_shape_checked.txt"
+                else:
+                    shape_template = "ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.attr_from_shape.txt"
+                parts.append(templates.render(shape_template,
+                    attr=attr, index=str(i), dim_index=str(dim_index), division=division))
+                found = True
+                break
+
+        # Case 2: attr appears in an operand text (e.g. constant(`@c.scale`))
+        if not found:
+            for i, assignment in enumerate(all_assignments):
+                for t in assignment.get('operand_texts', []):
+                    if f'@c.{attr}' in t:
+                        parts.append(templates.render(
+                            "ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.attr_from_constant.txt",
+                            attr=attr, index=str(i)))
+                        found = True
+                        break
+                if found:
+                    break
+
+        if not found:
+            root_index = num_assignments - 1
+            shape_template = "ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.attr_from_shape_checked.txt" if need_check else "ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.attr_from_shape.txt"
+            parts.append(templates.render(shape_template,
+                attr=attr, index=str(root_index), dim_index="0", division=""))
+
+    return '\n'.join(parts) + '\n' if parts else ""
+

+# Pins a literal-bounds slice to the matched enode's OpSlice payload, so a
+# same-shape slice at different offsets cannot match the rule.
+IOTA_DIM_CHECK = """    let iota_dim_{{index}} = match &lhs_enodes[{{index}}] {
+        Some(TensorOp::OpIota(data)) => data.split(':').next().unwrap_or(""),
+        _ => return false,
+    };
+    if iota_dim_{{index}} != "{{dim}}" {
+        return false;
+    }"""
+
+SLICE_PAYLOAD_CHECK = """    let slice_data_{{index}} = match &lhs_enodes[{{index}}] {
+        Some(TensorOp::OpSlice(data, _)) => data.as_str(),
+        _ => return false,
+    };
+    if slice_data_{{index}} != "{{payload}}" {
+        return false;
+    }"""
+
+
+# Pins a literal constant from the semantics to the matched e-class's value.
+# The pattern spells it as a variable, so there is no enode to read.
+CONST_VALUE_CHECK = """    {
+        let ec = lhs_eclasses[{{index}}];
+        let mut vals: Vec<i32> = egraph[ec].nodes.iter().filter_map(|en| match en {
+            TensorOp::OpConstant(v) => v.split(':').next().unwrap_or(v).parse::<i32>().ok(),
+            _ => None,
+        }).collect();
+        vals.sort();
+        vals.dedup();
+        if vals != vec![{{value}}] {
+            return false;
+        }
+    }"""
+
+
+def render_const_value_check(index, value):
+    return CONST_VALUE_CHECK.replace('{{index}}', str(index)).replace('{{value}}', str(value))
+
+
+def render_iota_dim_check(index, dim):
+    return IOTA_DIM_CHECK.replace("{{index}}", str(index)).replace("{{dim}}", str(dim))
+
+
+def render_slice_payload_check(index, payload):
+    return SLICE_PAYLOAD_CHECK.replace('{{index}}', str(index)).replace('{{payload}}', payload)
+

+def _find_dim_index_for_attr(shape_text, attr):
+    """Find the dimension index where @c.attr appears alone (not mixed with other @c. refs)."""
+    shape = shape_text.replace('`', '').replace(' ', '')
+    dims = shape.split(',')
+    for i, dim in enumerate(dims):
+        if f'@c.{attr}' in dim:
+            # Check this dimension only references this one attr
+            all_refs = re.findall(r'@c\.\w+', dim)
+            if len(all_refs) == 1:
+                return i
+    return -1

+def generate_precond_function(instruction_name, semantics_data, rhs_size, templates):
+    if not semantics_data:
+        return ""
+
+    assignments = semantics_data['assignments']
+    root_assignment = semantics_data['root_assignment']
+    comp_attrs = semantics_data['comp_attributes']
+
+    num_assignments = len(assignments)
+    # Generate comp attribute extraction
+    comp_attr_code = generate_all_comp_attr_extractions(root_assignment, comp_attrs, assignments, True, templates)
+
+    # Generate shape/dtype checks for all assignments
+    shape_checks = []
+    uses_lhs_enodes = False
+    for i, assignment in enumerate(assignments):
+        dtype_rust = map_dtype_to_rust(assignment['dtype'])
+        shape_expr = assignment['shape']
+
+        # Parse shape expression to extract dimensions
+        shape_expr = shape_expr.replace('`', '').replace(' ', '')
+
+        # Replace all @c.attr patterns with variable names
+        for attr in comp_attrs:
+            shape_expr = shape_expr.replace(f'@c.{attr}', attr)
+        shape_expr = re.sub(r'@c\.(\w+)', r'\1', shape_expr)
+
+        if ',' in shape_expr:
+            dims = [d.strip() for d in shape_expr.split(',')]
+        else:
+            dims = [shape_expr]
+
+        shape_vec = f"vec![{', '.join(dims)}]"
+
+        shape_check = templates.render("ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.shape_check.txt",
+                                       index=str(i),
+                                       shape_vec=shape_vec,
+                                       dtype=dtype_rust
+                                       )
+        shape_checks.append(shape_check)
+
+        slice_payload = assignment.get('slice_payload')
+        if slice_payload:
+            shape_checks.append(render_slice_payload_check(i, slice_payload))
+            uses_lhs_enodes = True
+        iota_dim = assignment.get('iota_dim')
+        if iota_dim is not None:
+            shape_checks.append(render_iota_dim_check(i, iota_dim))
+            uses_lhs_enodes = True
+
+        const_literal = assignment.get('const_literal')
+        if const_literal is not None:
+            try:
+                shape_checks.append(render_const_value_check(i, int(const_literal)))
+            except ValueError:
+                pass
+
+    shape_checks_code = '\n'.join(shape_checks)
+
+    precond = templates.render("ir2isa_rewrites.rs.IR2ISA_REWRITE_FUNCTIONS.precond.txt",
+                               instruction_name=instruction_name,
+                               num_assignments=str(num_assignments),
+                               comp_attr_code=comp_attr_code,
+                               shape_checks=shape_checks_code
+                               )
+    # A payload check reads the matched enode, so unmask the parameter.
+    if uses_lhs_enodes:
+        precond = precond.replace('_lhs_enodes', 'lhs_enodes')
+    return precond

+def generate_ir2isa_rust_functions(metadata, templates):
+    visitor = RustGeneratorVisitor()
+    semantics_data = visitor.visit(metadata.semantics_ast)
+    if not semantics_data:
+        return f"// Failed to parse semantics for {metadata.name}\n"
+
+    if metadata.comp_attrs:

+    precond = generate_precond_function(metadata.name, semantics_data, metadata.rhs_size, templates)

+    set_shapes = generate_set_shapes_function(

+    return f"{precond}\n\n{metadata_func}\n\n{set_shapes}\n\n"

+from .taidl.antlr4 import IDLV2Parser, IDLV2Visitor

+class RewriteRuleVisitor(IDLV2Visitor):
+    OP_MAP = {
+        'reshape': 'reshape_?', 'convert': 'convert_?', 'slice': 'slice_?',
+        'transpose': 'transpose_?', 'broadcast': 'broadcast_?', 'concat': 'concat_?',
+        'constant': 'constant_?', 'eye': 'eye_?', 'compare': 'compare_?',
+        'iota': 'iota_?',
+        'bitcast_convert': 'bitcvt',
+        'reduce_add': 'reduce-add_?',
+        'reduce_or': 'reduce-or_?',
+        'reduce_and': 'reduce-and_?',
+        'reduce_max': 'reduce-max_?',
+        'shift_left': 'shift-left', 'shift_right_logical': 'shift-right-logical',
+        'reverse': 'reverse_?',
+    }
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.pattern_stack = []
+        self.variable_counter = 0
+        self.input_variables = {}
+        self.parameter_variables = {}
+        self.variable_definitions = {}
+        self.root_variable = None
+        self.variable_usage_count = set()
+
+    def get_next_variable(self):
+        var_name = f"?{chr(ord('a') + self.variable_counter)}"
+        self.variable_counter += 1
+        return var_name
+
+    def substitute_params(self, pattern, substitutions):
+        result = pattern
+        for old_var, new_var in substitutions.items():
+            result = result.replace(old_var, new_var)
+        return result
+
+    def visitModule(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.ModuleContext):
+        self.visitChildren(ctx)
+        if self.root_variable and self.root_variable in self.variable_definitions:
+            return self.variable_definitions[self.root_variable]
+        elif self.pattern_stack:
+            return self.pattern_stack[-1]
+        return None
+
+    def get_parameter_variables(self):
+        sorted_params = sorted(self.parameter_variables.items(), key=lambda x: x[0])
+        return [var for param_num, var in sorted_params]
+
+    def visitInstruction(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.InstructionContext):
+        lhs_name = ctx.IDENTIFIER().getText()
+        op_name = ctx.OPERATION().getText()
+
+        is_root = ctx.ROOT() is not None
+        if is_root:
+            self.root_variable = lhs_name
+
+        if op_name == 'parameter':
+            if ctx.operands():
+                operand_info = self.visit(ctx.operands())
+                if operand_info:
+                    param_num = int(operand_info[0][0])
+                    var = self.get_next_variable()
+                    self.parameter_variables[param_num] = var
+                    self.variable_definitions[lhs_name] = var
+                    return var
+
+        # Check if this instruction has any IDENTIFIER operands (references to other SSA values).
+        # Leaf ops like constant(`@c.scale`) have no identifier operands -- they should
+        # become variables in the pattern to avoid egg's 0-arity metadata matching issue.
+        has_identifier_operand = False
+        operand_info = []
+        if ctx.operands():
+            operand_info = self.visit(ctx.operands())
+            for operand_value, operand_type in operand_info:
+                if operand_type == 'IDENTIFIER' and operand_value in self.variable_definitions:
+                    has_identifier_operand = True
+                    break
+
+        if not has_identifier_operand and not is_root:
+            var = self.get_next_variable()
+            self.variable_definitions[lhs_name] = var
+            self.pattern_stack.append(var)
+            return var
+
+        operand_patterns = []
+        for operand_value, operand_type in operand_info:
+            if operand_type == 'IDENTIFIER':
+                if operand_value in self.variable_definitions:
+                    pattern = self.variable_definitions[operand_value]
+
+                    if operand_value in self.variable_usage_count:
+                        substitutions = {}
+                        for param_var in self.parameter_variables.values():
+                            if param_var in pattern:
+                                fresh_var = self.get_next_variable()
+                                substitutions[param_var] = fresh_var
+                        if substitutions:
+                            pattern = self.substitute_params(pattern, substitutions)
+                    else:
+                        self.variable_usage_count.add(operand_value)
+
+                    operand_patterns.append(pattern)
+                else:
+                    var = self.get_next_variable()
+                    operand_patterns.append(var)
+
+        rewrite_op_name = self.OP_MAP.get(op_name, op_name)
+        pattern = f"({rewrite_op_name} {' '.join(operand_patterns)})" if operand_patterns else f"({rewrite_op_name})"
+
+        self.variable_definitions[lhs_name] = pattern
+        self.pattern_stack.append(pattern)
+
+        return pattern
+
+    def visitOperands(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.OperandsContext):
+        operand_list = []
+        for operand_ctx in ctx.operand():
+            operand_info = self.visit(operand_ctx)
+            operand_list.append(operand_info)
+        return operand_list
+
+    def visitOperand(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.OperandContext):
+        value_ctx = ctx.value()
+        value_text = value_ctx.getText()
+
+        if value_ctx.INT():
+            operand_type = 'INT'
+        elif value_ctx.IDENTIFIER():
+            operand_type = 'IDENTIFIER'
+        elif value_ctx.EXPRESSION():
+            operand_type = 'EXPRESSION'
+        else:
+            operand_type = 'UNKNOWN'
+
+        return (value_text, operand_type)
+
+    def visitAttributes(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.AttributesContext):
+        attributes_list = []
+        for attribute_ctx in ctx.attribute():
+            attr_info = self.visit(attribute_ctx)
+            attributes_list.append(attr_info)
+        return attributes_list
+
+    def visitAttribute(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.AttributeContext):
+        # an attribute name may lex as OPERATION, e.g. slice=
+        attr_name = (ctx.IDENTIFIER() or ctx.OPERATION()).getText()
+        attr_value_info = self.visit(ctx.attributeValue())
+        attr_value, attr_type = attr_value_info
+        return (attr_name, attr_value, attr_type)
+
+    def visitAttributeValue(self, ctx: IDLV2Parser.AttributeValueContext):
+        if ctx.braceList():
+            brace_info = self.visit(ctx.braceList())
+            return (brace_info, 'BRACELIST')
+        elif ctx.value():
+            value_ctx = ctx.value()
+            value_text = value_ctx.getText()
+
+            if value_ctx.INT():
+                value_type = 'INT'
+            elif value_ctx.IDENTIFIER():
+                value_type = 'IDENTIFIER'
+            elif value_ctx.EXPRESSION():
+                value_type = 'EXPRESSION'
+            else:
+                value_type = 'UNKNOWN'
+
+            return (value_text, value_type)
+
+
+def generate_rewrite_rule(metadata, templates):
+    """Generate a single rewrite rule using template"""
+    visitor = RewriteRuleVisitor()
+    lhs_pattern = visitor.visit(metadata.semantics_ast)
+    parameter_vars = visitor.get_parameter_variables()
+    kebab_name = metadata.name.replace('_', '-')
+
+    # An instruction with no operands still has a pattern; only an unparseable
+    # semantics has none, and a rule built from one would panic at construction.
+    if not lhs_pattern:
+        raise ValueError(f"{metadata.name}: semantics produced no rewrite pattern")
+
+    # Generate RHS with or without _? suffix
+    rhs = f"({kebab_name}_? {' '.join(parameter_vars)})" if metadata.has_comp_attrs else f"({kebab_name} {' '.join(parameter_vars)})"
+
+    # Calculate padding to align the '=>' at column 20
+    padding = ' ' * (19 - len(kebab_name))
+
+    return templates.render(
+        "ir2isa_rewrites.txt.IR2ISA_REWRITE_RULES.rule.txt",
+        kebab_name=kebab_name,
+        padding=padding,
+        lhs_pattern=lhs_pattern,
+        rhs=rhs
+    )
+
+
+def generate_ir2isa_rewrites_txt_file(backend_gen_dir: str, instruction_metadata_list):
+    """Template ir2isa_rewrites.txt from generic file"""
+    templates = get_backend_template_loader()
+
+    # Read generic file
+    rewrites_file = os.path.join(backend_gen_dir, 'src', 'isel', 'rewrites', 'ir2isa_rewrites.txt')
+    with open(rewrites_file, 'r') as f:
+        content = f.read()
+
+    # Generate all rewrite rules
+    rules = []
+    for metadata in instruction_metadata_list:
+        rule = generate_rewrite_rule(metadata, templates)
+        rules.append(rule)
+
+    # Join rules with newlines
+    all_rules = '\n'.join(rules)
+
+    # Replace placeholder
+    content = content.replace('{{IR2ISA_REWRITE_RULES}}', all_rules)
+
+    # Write back
+    with open(rewrites_file, 'w') as f:
+        f.write(content)

+import os
+import re
+from .template_loader import get_backend_template_loader

+
+def to_camel_case(snake_str):
+    return ''.join(word.capitalize() for word in snake_str.split('_'))
+
+
+def extract_addr_var(expr):
+    match = re.search(r'@a\.(\w+)', expr)
+    return match.group(1) if match else None
+
+
+def extract_size_expr(expr):
+    if isinstance(expr, int):
+        return str(expr)
+    result = re.sub(r'@c\.', '', str(expr))
+    return result.strip()
+
+
+def generate_get_h_method(index, addr_vars, size_exprs, templates):
+    range_pairs = []
+    for addr_var, size_expr in zip(addr_vars, size_exprs):
+        # Literal integer addresses (e.g. 0) need to be wrapped as known constants
+        if addr_var.isdigit() or (addr_var.startswith('-') and addr_var[1:].isdigit()):
+            addr_expr = f"MAKE_INT_KNOWN({addr_var})"
+            range_pairs.append(f"{{{addr_expr}, MAKE_INT_KNOWN({addr_var} + {size_expr})}}")
+        else:
+            range_pairs.append(f"{{{addr_var}, MAKE_SUM({addr_var}, {size_expr})}}")
+    ranges = ", ".join(range_pairs)
+    return templates.render("instructions.h.INSTRUCTION_CLASSES.get_h_method.txt",
+                            index=index,
+                            ranges=ranges)
+
+
+def require_addressable(op_name, kind, addr_vars):
+    """Every operand must emit a get_h range: constraint.cc indexes them as
+    0=lhs and i+1=rhs_i, so skipping one shifts every later operand's index."""
+    if not any(a for a in addr_vars if a and a != '0'):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{op_name}: {kind} operand has no address variable in any dimension; "
+            f"give it an @a.<attr> address instead of a literal 0")
+
+
+def generate_instruction_class(instruction, templates):
+    """Generate C++ instruction class from instruction definition"""
+    class_name = to_camel_case(instruction.instruction)
+    op_name = instruction.instruction
+    comp_attrs = instruction.comp_attr
+    params = instruction.parameters
+
+    # Generate members
+    comp_attr_members = ""
+    for attr in comp_attrs:
+        comp_attr_members += f"  int64 {attr};\n"
+
+    addr_var_members = "\n"
+    for param in params:
+        addr_var_members += f"  IntVar *{param} = MAKE_INT_VAR(INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX);\n"
+
+    # Generate get_h methods: output first (get_h0), then inputs (get_h1, get_h2, ...)
+    get_h_methods = ""
+    get_h_cases = ""
+    h_index = 0
+
+    # Process outputs
+    for output in instruction.instr_outputs:
+        _, addr_expr_list, size_expr_list = output
+        addr_vars = [extract_addr_var(a) if isinstance(a, str) and '@a.' in a else str(a)
+                     for a in addr_expr_list]
+        size_exprs = [extract_size_expr(s) for s in size_expr_list]
+
+        require_addressable(op_name, "output", addr_vars)
+        get_h_methods += generate_get_h_method(h_index, addr_vars, size_exprs, templates)
+        get_h_cases += templates.render(
+            "instructions.h.INSTRUCTION_CLASSES.get_h_case.txt", index=h_index)
+        h_index += 1
+
+    # Process inputs
+    for inp in instruction.instr_inputs:
+        _, addr_expr_list, size_expr_list = inp
+        addr_vars = [extract_addr_var(a) if isinstance(a, str) and '@a.' in a else str(a)
+                     for a in addr_expr_list]
+        size_exprs = [extract_size_expr(s) for s in size_expr_list]
+
+        require_addressable(op_name, "input", addr_vars)
+        get_h_methods += generate_get_h_method(h_index, addr_vars, size_exprs, templates)
+        get_h_cases += templates.render(
+            "instructions.h.INSTRUCTION_CLASSES.get_h_case.txt", index=h_index)
+        h_index += 1
+
+    # Generate constructor parameters
+    comp_attr_params = ""
+    if comp_attrs:
+        comp_attr_params = ", " + ", ".join(f"int64 {attr}" for attr in comp_attrs)
+
+    # Generate constructor initialization
+    comp_attr_init = ""
+    if comp_attrs:
+        comp_attr_init = ", " + ", ".join(f"{attr}({attr})" for attr in comp_attrs)
+
+    # No validations needed
+    validations = ""
+    str_bound_checks = ""
+
+    str_format = ""
+    for attr in comp_attrs:
+        if str_format:
+            str_format += ", "
+        str_format += f"{attr} = \" + std::to_string({attr}) + \""
+    for param in params:
+        if str_format:
+            str_format += ", "
+        str_format += f"{param} = \" + std::to_string({param}->Value()) + \""
+
+    # Generate get_int_var list
+    get_int_var_list = ", ".join(params)
+
+    # Generate inplace override for all instructions
+    inplace_vec = ", ".join("true" if v else "false" for v in instruction.inplace)
+    inplace_override = templates.render("instructions.h.INSTRUCTION_CLASSES.inplace_override.txt",
+                                        INPLACE_VEC=inplace_vec)
+
+    # Generate complete class using template
+    return templates.render("instructions.h.INSTRUCTION_CLASSES.class.txt",
+                            CLASS_NAME=class_name,
+                            OP_NAME=op_name,
+                            COMP_ATTR_MEMBERS=comp_attr_members,
+                            ADDR_VAR_MEMBERS=addr_var_members,
+                            GET_H_METHODS=get_h_methods,
+                            COMP_ATTR_PARAMS=comp_attr_params,
+                            COMP_ATTR_INIT=comp_attr_init,
+                            CONSTRUCTOR_VALIDATIONS=validations,
+                            STR_BOUND_CHECKS=str_bound_checks,
+                            STR_FORMAT=str_format,
+                            GET_H_CASES=get_h_cases,
+                            GET_INT_VAR_LIST=get_int_var_list,
+                            INPLACE_OVERRIDE=inplace_override)
+
+
+def generate_instructions_file(backend_gen_dir, instructions, data_models):
+    """Template instructions.h from generic file"""
+    templates = get_backend_template_loader()
+
+    # Read generic template file
+    generic_file = os.path.join(backend_gen_dir, 'cpp', 'malloc', 'include', 'instructions.h')
+    with open(generic_file, 'r') as f:

+
+    # Replace placeholder

+
+    # Write back
+    with open(generic_file, 'w') as f:
+        f.write(content)

+"""Instruction set definitions for TAIDLv2"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
+
+from antlr4 import CommonTokenStream, InputStream
+
+from .data_model import DataModel
+from .antlr4 import IDLV2Lexer, IDLV2Parser
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Instruction:
+    instruction: str
+    comp_attr: List[str]
+    parameters: List[str]
+    constraints: List[str]
+    data_models: List[DataModel]
+    cost: str
+    update: List[str]
+
+    instr_inputs: List[Tuple[str, List[str], List[str]]]
+    instr_outputs: List[Tuple[str, List[str], List[str]]]
+    instr_semantics_str: str
+    instr_semantics_ast: Optional[IDLV2Parser.ModuleContext]
+    inplace: List[bool]
+
+    def __init__(self, instruction: str, comp_attr: List[str], addr_attr: List[str], constraints: List[str], cost: str, update: List[str], data_models: List[DataModel]):
+        self.instruction = instruction.replace(" ", "_")
+        self.comp_attr = comp_attr
+        self.parameters = addr_attr
+        self.constraints = constraints
+        self.cost = cost
+        self.update = update
+        self.data_models = data_models
+        self.instr_inputs = []
+        self.instr_outputs = []
+        self.instr_semantics_str = ""
+        self.instr_semantics_ast = None
+        self.inplace = []
+
+    def find_data_model(self, name: str) -> DataModel:
+        for model in self.data_models:
+            if (model.var_name == name):
+                break
+        else:
+            model = None
+        assert (model != None), f"Data buffer '{name}' not found"
+        return model
+
+    def set_inputs(self, inputs: List[Tuple[str, List[str], List[str]]]):
+        self.instr_inputs = inputs
+        if not self.inplace:
+            self.inplace = [False] * len(inputs)
+
+    def set_outputs(self, outputs: List[Tuple[str, List[str], List[str]]]):
+        self.instr_outputs = outputs
+
+    def set_inplace(self, inplace_operands: List[bool]):
+        """Mark which RHS operands are inplace (overwritten by the instruction).
+        Length must match the number of inputs."""
+        self.inplace = inplace_operands
+
+    def add_semantics(self, semantics: str):
+        self.instr_semantics_str = semantics
+        self.instr_semantics_ast = None
+        if semantics and semantics.strip():
+            self.instr_semantics_ast = self._parse_semantics(semantics)
+
+    def _parse_semantics(self, semantics: str):
+        """Parse semantics into AST eagerly to catch syntax errors early"""
+        input_stream = InputStream(semantics)
+        lexer = IDLV2Lexer(input_stream)
+        stream = CommonTokenStream(lexer)
+        parser = IDLV2Parser(stream)
+        tree = parser.module()
+        if parser.getNumberOfSyntaxErrors() > 0:
+            raise SyntaxError(f"Failed to parse semantics for instruction '{self.instruction}'")
+        return tree
+
+    def add_constraints(self, constraints: str):
+        lines = constraints.strip().split("\n")
+        self.constraints = [line for line in lines if line.strip()]

+"""Template management for backend code generation
+
+Provides a clean interface for loading and using code templates without
+mutable global variables.
+"""
+
+import os
+from typing import Dict
+
+
+class TemplateLoader:
+    """Manages loading and caching of templates for code generation"""
+
+    def __init__(self, template_dir: str):
+        """
+        Initialize template loader
+
+        Args:
+            template_dir: Directory containing template files
+        """
+        self.template_dir = template_dir
+        self._cache: Dict[str, str] = {}
+
+    def load(self, template_file: str) -> str:
+        """
+        Load a template file
+
+        Args:
+            template_file: Name of the template file
+
+        Returns:
+            Template content as string
+        """
+        if template_file not in self._cache:
+            file_path = os.path.join(self.template_dir, template_file)
+            with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
+                self._cache[template_file] = f.read()
+        return self._cache[template_file]
+
+    def render(self, template_file: str, **kwargs) -> str:
+        """
+        Load and render a template with the given variables
+
+        Args:
+            template_file: Name of the template file
+            **kwargs: Template variables
+
+        Returns:
+            Rendered template content
+        """
+        template = self.load(template_file)
+        result = template
+        for key, value in kwargs.items():
+            placeholder = f"{{{{{key}}}}}"
+            result = result.replace(placeholder, str(value))
+        return result
+
+
+def get_backend_template_loader() -> TemplateLoader:
+    """Get a template loader for backend templates"""
+    template_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'templates')
+    return TemplateLoader(template_dir)

+"""Fold the measurements of a full.sh run into a copy of the paper's tables.
+
+Usage: python evaluation/collect_results.py --run-dir plots/full_run_<timestamp>
+"""
+import argparse
+import csv
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+import time
+
+REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+
+PHASES = {
+    'applier': 'M2_Rewriter',
+    'extractor': 'M3_Extractor',
+    'csp_gen': 'M5_CSPGen',
+    'csp_solve': 'MX_Solver',
+}
+NODE_BIN = 10
+
+# fixed table set; widths align the "(4.1)" row block regardless of run size
+TABLE_NAMES = ['gemmini_swlib_perf.csv', 'gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv',
+               'nki_stress_compile.csv', 'nki_coverage.csv']
+NAME_WIDTH = max(len(n) for n in TABLE_NAMES)
+COUNT_WIDTH = 4
+
+
+def write_csv(path, header, rows, updated=None):
+    """Write one paper table and print its aligned (4.1) row."""
+    with open(path, 'w', newline='') as f:
+        w = csv.writer(f)
+        w.writerow(header)
+        w.writerows(rows)
+    if updated is None:
+        updated = len(rows)
+    name = os.path.basename(path)
+    print(f'      {name:<{NAME_WIDTH}} | {len(rows):>{COUNT_WIDTH}} rows | '
+          f'{updated:>{COUNT_WIDTH}} updated')
+    return 1
+
+
+def collect_swlib(run_dir, sweep_csv):
+    """Verilator cycle counts for the 15 Gemmini kernels."""
+    if not os.path.exists(sweep_csv):
+        print('      Skipped gemmini_swlib_perf.csv -- no sweep output')
+        return 0
+
+    rows = []
+    with open(sweep_csv) as f:
+        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
+            if not row['cycles'] or not row['baseline_cycles']:
+                print(f"      Skipped gemmini_swlib_perf.csv -- {row['label']} is incomplete")
+                return 0
+            rows.append((row['label'], row['class'],
+                         int(row['cycles']), int(row['baseline_cycles'])))
+
+    return write_csv(os.path.join(run_dir, 'gemmini_swlib_perf.csv'),
+                      ['kernel', 'class', 'act_cycles', 'baseline_cycles'], rows)
+
+
+def parse_stats_log(path):
+    """Per-kernel phase timings in ms, keyed by the kernel name in the header."""
+    per_kernel, current = {}, None
+    with open(path) as f:
+        for line in f:
+            header = re.match(r'=== (\S+) ===', line)
+            if header:
+                current = header.group(1)
+                per_kernel[current] = {}
+                continue
+            stat = re.match(r'\[STATS\] (\w+)=([0-9.]+)(m?s)', line)
+            if stat and current is not None:
+                ms = float(stat.group(2)) * (1.0 if stat.group(3) == 'ms' else 1000.0)
+                per_kernel[current][stat.group(1)] = ms
+    return per_kernel
+
+
+def count_hlo_nodes(path):
+    """HLO instruction count: one assignment per line."""
+    with open(path) as f:
+        return sum(1 for line in f if ' = ' in line)
+
+
+def collect_stress_time(run_dir, stats_log, hlo_dir):
+    """Compilation time per stress kernel, one row each, ordered by size."""
+    if not os.path.exists(stats_log):
+        print('      Skipped nki_stress_compile.csv -- no stats log')
+        return 0
+
+    rows = []
+    for kernel, stats in parse_stats_log(stats_log).items():
+        hlo = os.path.join(hlo_dir, kernel + '.gen.hlo')
+        if 'total_time' not in stats or not os.path.exists(hlo):
+            continue
+        phases = {name: stats.get(stat, 0.0) for name, stat in PHASES.items()}
+        rest = max(stats['total_time'] - sum(phases.values()), 0.0)
+        rows.append([kernel, count_hlo_nodes(hlo)]
+                    + [round(phases[name], 2) for name in PHASES]
+                    + [round(rest, 2)])
+
+    rows.sort(key=lambda row: row[1])
+    return write_csv(os.path.join(run_dir, 'nki_stress_compile.csv'),
+                      ['kernel', 'nodes'] + list(PHASES) + ['rest'], rows)
+
+
+def collect_fuzz_time(run_dir, stats_log, summary_csv):
+    """Compilation time by kernel size, averaged within node-count buckets."""
+    if not os.path.exists(stats_log):
+        print('      Skipped gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv -- no stats log')
+        return 0
+
+    nodes_of = {}
+    with open(summary_csv) as f:
+        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
+            nodes_of[row['filename'].replace('.gen.hlo', '')] = int(row['total_nodes'])
+
+    buckets = {}
+    for kernel, stats in parse_stats_log(stats_log).items():
+        if kernel not in nodes_of or 'total_time' not in stats:
+            continue
+        nodes = nodes_of[kernel]
+        buckets.setdefault(nodes // NODE_BIN, []).append((nodes, stats))
+
+    rows = []
+    for key in sorted(buckets):
+        group = buckets[key]
+        mean = {name: sum(s.get(stat, 0.0) for _, s in group) / len(group)
+                for name, stat in PHASES.items()}
+        total = sum(s['total_time'] for _, s in group) / len(group)
+        rest = max(total - sum(mean.values()), 0.0)
+        rows.append([round(sum(n for n, _ in group) / len(group))]
+                    + [round(mean[name], 2) for name in PHASES]
+                    + [round(rest, 2)])
+
+    return write_csv(os.path.join(run_dir, 'gemmini_fuzz_compile.csv'),
+                      ['nodes'] + list(PHASES) + ['rest'], rows)
+
+
+def collect_nki_coverage(run_dir, coverage_log, reran_neuronxcc):
+    """Update the compilation status of every kernel this run actually saw."""
+    if not os.path.exists(coverage_log):
+        print('      Skipped nki_coverage.csv -- no coverage log')
+        return 0
+
+    measured = {}
+    with open(coverage_log) as f:
+        for line in f:
+            m = re.match(r'COVERAGE (\S+) act=(\w+) neuronx=(\w+)', line)
+            if m:
+                measured[m.group(1).replace('.gen.hlo', '')] = (
+                    m.group(2) == 'True', m.group(3) == 'True')
+
+    path = os.path.join(run_dir, 'nki_coverage.csv')
+    with open(path) as f:
+        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
+
+    for row in rows:
+        if row['kernel'] not in measured:
+            continue
+        act, neuronx = measured[row['kernel']]
+        row['act'] = int(act)
+        if reran_neuronxcc:
+            row['neuronx_cc'] = int(neuronx)
+        row['speedup'] = 1.0 if int(row['act']) and int(row['neuronx_cc']) else 'NA'
+
+    return write_csv(path, ['kernel', 'family', 'neuronx_cc', 'act', 'speedup'],
+                      [[r['kernel'], r['family'], r['neuronx_cc'], r['act'], r['speedup']]
+                       for r in rows], updated=len(measured))
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument('--run-dir', required=True,
+                    help='Directory seeded from plots/paper_data/.')
+    ap.add_argument('--rerun-neuronxcc', action='store_true',
+                    help='The run refreshed the neuronx-cc baseline too.')
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    if not os.path.isdir(args.run_dir):
+        sys.exit(f'No such run directory: {args.run_dir}')
+
+    start = int(time.time())
+    print()
+    print('(4.1) Updating the measured rows of the paper tables...')
+    written = 0
+    written += collect_swlib(args.run_dir,
+                              os.path.join(REPO, 'evaluation', 'gemmini', 'results', 'swlib.csv'))
+    written += collect_fuzz_time(args.run_dir,
+                                  os.path.join(REPO, 'compiled_asm', 'gemmini', 'fuzz', 'stats.log'),
+                                  os.path.join(REPO, 'kernels', 'gemmini', 'summary.csv'))
+    written += collect_stress_time(args.run_dir,
+                                    os.path.join(REPO, 'compiled_asm', 'nki', 'stress', 'stats.log'),
+                                    os.path.join(REPO, 'kernels', 'nki', 'stress'))
+    written += collect_nki_coverage(args.run_dir,
+                                     os.path.join(REPO, 'compiled_asm', 'nki', 'coverage_results.log'),
+                                     args.rerun_neuronxcc)
+
+    print(f'Completed collecting results: {written} tables written.')
+    rel_run_dir = os.path.relpath(os.path.abspath(args.run_dir), REPO)
+    print(f'Tables saved to {rel_run_dir}.')
+
+    end = int(time.time())
+    timings = os.environ.get('ACT_RUN_TIMINGS')
+    if timings:
+        with open(timings, 'a') as f:
+            f.write(f'Results\t{start}\t{end}\t{written} tables written\n')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+  echo "         and a few syscalls. If this option is not set, binaries will be"

+  echo " BINARY  The RISCV binary that you want to run. This can either be the"
+  echo '         name of a program in `software/gemmini-rocc-tests`, or it can'
+  echo "         be the full path to a binary you compiled."

+  echo "         $0 resnet50"
+  echo "         $0 --pk mvin_mvout"
+  echo "         $0 path/to/binary-baremetal"
+  echo
+  echo 'Note:    Run this command after running `scripts/build-spike.sh`.'
+  echo
+  echo "Note:    On Spike, cycle counts, SoC counter values, and performance"
+  echo "         statistics are all meaningless. Use Spike only to check if your"

+"""Fill each kernel template with the assembly ACT compiled for it.
+
+Reads evaluation/gemmini/templates/swlib/<K>.c, replaces its /* ACT_INSTRUCTIONS */
+placeholder with ACT's assembly lowered to RoCC calls, and writes
+evaluation/gemmini/tests/<K>.c.
+"""
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+from gemmini_rocc import (ACC_ACCUMULATE_BIT, ACC_BIT, ACC_FULL_WIDTH_BIT, GARBAGE_ADDR,
+                          lower_asm)
+
+ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "..", ".."))
+ASM_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "compiled_asm", "gemmini", "swlib")
+TEMPLATE_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "evaluation", "gemmini", "templates", "swlib")
+OUT_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "evaluation", "gemmini", "tests")
+MARKER = "/* ACT_INSTRUCTIONS */"
+
+# Which template buffer each of ACT's dram roles refers to. Inputs are A, B, C, D in
+# order and the output is OUT, except where a template names them otherwise.
+ROLES = {"input0": "A", "input1": "B", "input2": "C", "input3": "D", "output0": "OUT"}
+PER_KERNEL = {
+    "AxB_plus_C": {"input2": "D"},
+    "broadcast": {"constant0": "ones"},
+    "reduce": {"constant0": "ones"},
+    "reverse": {"constant0": "anti"},
+}
+
+KERNELS = ["A_plus_B", "A_plus_B_plus_C", "A_plus_B_plus_C_plus_D", "AxB", "AxB_plus_AxC",
+           "AxB_plus_C", "AxB_plus_C_plus_D", "AxBxC", "AxBxC_plus_A", "AxBxC_plus_D",
+           "AxBxCxA", "AxBxCxD", "broadcast", "reduce", "reverse"]
+
+
+# --- RoCC instruction stream -> C statements ----------------------------------
+
+def _raw_local(addr):
+    if addr.space == "garbage":
+        return GARBAGE_ADDR
+    if addr.space == "acc":
+        v = addr.index | ACC_BIT
+        if addr.accumulate:
+            v |= ACC_ACCUMULATE_BIT
+        if addr.full_width:
+            v |= ACC_FULL_WIDTH_BIT
+        return v
+    return addr.index
+
+
+def emit_instructions(instrs, ref):
+    """Translate ACT's RoCC stream to gemmini_extended_* statements, addressed by the
+    template's own buffer names and ACT's own raw scratchpad/accumulator numbers.
+
+    mvin/mvout are asynchronous DMA: a kernel that round-trips a value through DRAM (mvout it,
+    then mvin it back, as AxB_plus_C_plus_D does instead of fusing into the accumulator) needs
+    an explicit fence between the two or the read can race the write. Inserted here, once, only
+    when a later mvin/mvin2 actually reads the same dram role an earlier mvout wrote.
+    """
+    lines = []
+    pending_writes = set()
+    for instr in instrs:
+        op = instr.op
+        if op in ("mvin", "mvin2"):
+            dram, local = instr.operands
+            cols, rows = instr.shape
+            if dram.index in pending_writes:
+                lines.append("  gemmini_fence();")
+                pending_writes.clear()
+            func = "gemmini_extended_mvin" if op == "mvin" else "gemmini_extended_mvin2"
+            lines.append(f"  {func}({ref[dram.index]}, {_raw_local(local)}u, {cols}, {rows});")
+        elif op == "mvout":
+            dram, local = instr.operands
+            cols, rows = instr.shape
+            lines.append(f"  gemmini_extended_mvout({ref[dram.index]}, {_raw_local(local)}u, "
+                         f"{cols}, {rows});")
+            pending_writes.add(dram.index)
+        elif op == "preload":
+            bd, c = instr.operands
+            bd_cols, bd_rows, c_cols, c_rows = instr.shape
+            lines.append(f"  gemmini_extended_preload({_raw_local(bd)}u, {_raw_local(c)}u, "
+                         f"{bd_cols}, {bd_rows}, {c_cols}, {c_rows});")
+        elif op == "compute_preloaded":
+            a, bd = instr.operands
+            a_cols, a_rows, bd_cols, bd_rows = instr.shape
+            lines.append(f"  gemmini_extended_compute_preloaded({_raw_local(a)}u, "
+                         f"{_raw_local(bd)}u, {a_cols}, {a_rows}, {bd_cols}, {bd_rows});")
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"no C emission for RoCC op {op}")
+    return lines
+
+
+# --- driver --------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def generate(kernel):
+    template = os.path.join(TEMPLATE_DIR, f"{kernel}.c")
+    text = open(template).read()
+    if MARKER not in text:
+        raise ValueError(f"{template}: no {MARKER} placeholder")
+
+    program = lower_asm(os.path.join(ASM_DIR, f"{kernel}.asm.py"))
+    try:
+        lines = emit_instructions(program.instrs, dict(ROLES, **PER_KERNEL.get(kernel, {})))
+    except KeyError as e:
+        raise ValueError(f"{kernel}: dram role {e} has no buffer in the template") from e
+
+    indent = " " * (text.index(MARKER) - text.rfind("\n", 0, text.index(MARKER)) - 1)
+    body = ("\n" + indent).join(line.strip() for line in lines)
+
+    text = f"// Generated from templates/swlib/{kernel}.c. Do not edit.\n\n" + text
+
+    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
+    out_path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, f"{kernel}.c")
+    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
+        f.write(text.replace(MARKER, body, 1))
+    return out_path
+
+
+def main():
+    """Stage every kernel's C file quietly; return how many were staged."""
+    names = sys.argv[1:] or KERNELS
+    staged = 0
+    for name in names:
+        asm_path = os.path.join(ASM_DIR, f"{name}.asm.py")
+        if not os.path.exists(asm_path):
+            # compiled_asm/gemmini/swlib is rebuilt by the ACT backend, out of this
+            # script's control -- a kernel can be renamed or merged away between runs.
+            print(f"      skipped {name}: no {os.path.relpath(asm_path, ROOT)}")
+            continue
+        generate(name)
+        staged += 1
+    return staged
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
